name: New Silk Road Cloud Computing Center
developer: Xinjiang Yunzhi Digital Network Co., Ltd.
notes: Urumqi government reported the Xinjiang Economic and Technological Development Zone/Toutunhe facility was selected as a 2025 national green data center, operated by Xinjiang Yunzhi Digital Network, with indirect evaporative cooling, smart micro-modular rooms and long-term PUE below 1.2.

name: Wanjie Xinjiang Jiangsuan 10,000-card hub AI computing center
developer: Urumqi Jiangsuan Technology Development Co., Ltd. / Beijing Wanjie Data Technology
notes: Xinjiang government reported Beijing Wanjie began construction in September 2025 in the Lianghe area of Urumqi Economic and Technological Development Zone/Toutunhe; phase 1 plans 10000P by October 2026 and phase 2 targets 20000P by 2027, using an integrated compute, renewable power and virtual power plant model with a self-built 220 kV substation.

name: Wangan Green Computing Technology Park / fusion computing center
developer: Xinjiang Zhongke Leibrao Zhishuan Technology Co., Ltd.
notes: Xinjiang government said the Wanjiang Green Computing Technology Park fusion computing center had been completed and put into operation in Urumqi Economic and Technological Development Zone/Toutunhe. The district had attracted five computing firms, built two A-grade general-purpose computing data centers, and reached 1021P of operating compute.

name: Xinjiang national-level fusion computing center plan
developer: Xinjiang / Urumqi public-sector and academic sponsors
notes: Xinjiang commerce department reposted Urumqi media coverage of a proposed national-level fusion computing center in Urumqi combining supercomputing, AI computing and data-storage capacity, with an end-2024 concept target above 500P of integrated compute.

Searches for Wujiaqu/Fifth Division/Sixth Division data center, cloud computing and AI computing projects found official city pages and regional Urumqi/Changji compute projects nearby, but no verified public data-center facility or active project inside Wujiaqu Shi.

name: Xinjiang Ruicun AI Computing Center, Qingshuihe supporting park
developer: Xinjiang Ruicun Information Technology Service Co., Ltd.
notes: Huocheng County government reported the May 12 groundbreaking in Qingshuihe supporting park for a roughly RMB 2 billion AI computing center, planned at 5000P, using modular construction and green energy-saving technology, with first-phase compute expected to be lit by late October 2025 and full completion within two years.

name: Horgos Tianyi Cloud International Big Data Center
developer: China Telecom / Tianyi Cloud interests
notes: Yili prefecture government reported that after completion the Horgos Tianyi Cloud International Big Data Center planned to apply for an international Internet dedicated channel and cross-border access acceleration platform, positioning it as part of the Digital Silk Road at the border port.

name: Huawei Baoshan Big Data Center / Baoshan Cloud
developer: Baoshan municipal government / Huawei Cloud
notes: People's Daily Yunnan reported Huawei Baoshan Big Data Center had entered operation as an important Huawei enterprise-cloud node and global sample site serving western Yunnan. Xinhua later described Baoshan's unified government cloud, built in 2018, carrying city/county/township government systems and data storage with nearly 70 percent of non-secret self-built information systems migrated.

name: Chuxiong City Digital Two-Asia AI Computing Center project
developer: Chuxiong City investment-promotion authorities / to be determined
notes: Chuxiong City investment-promotion page lists a planned 30000 sqm AI computing center and power support project with 3300 cabinets at 7.5 kW each, total power not above 25000 kW, target compute of 5000P, and intended A-grade/green/reliability/security certifications.

name: Dali Prefecture Big Data Center and Canger Cloud phase II
developer: Dali Prefecture / China Mobile Yunnan Dali branch / China System Yunnan
notes: People's Daily Yunnan reported the Dali Prefecture Big Data Center and Canger Cloud phase II main structure was completed. Earlier China News coverage said phase I was built in April 2013, with 6373.87 sqm, more than 700 cabinets and capacity for over 5000 servers, hosting e-government, smart-city and sector systems.

name: Longzhiyin Dali Midu AI Computing Industrial Park
developer: Shanghai Longzhiyin Technology (Group) Co., Ltd.
notes: IDCE reported Shanghai Longzhiyin signed with Dali Prefecture and Midu County on December 13, 2024 for a RMB 5 billion AI computing industrial park with 6000 racks averaging 15 kW, 20000P compute and 500 PB storage after completion; capacity_mw is inferred from the reported 6000 racks x 15 kW average.

Searches found Dehong/Ruili digital-economy, cross-border e-commerce and logistics big-data activity, including Ruili port logistics data platforms, but no verified public standalone data center, AI computing center or hyperscale/colocation project in Dehong prefecture.

name: Tianyi Cloud Big Data Center, Diqing
developer: China Telecom / Tianyi Cloud
notes: People's Daily Yunnan and Xinhua Yunnan reported that in Diqing, Tianyi Cloud Big Data Center provides cloud services including elastic computing, cloud storage, databases, network security and big-data analytics for multiple industries and scenarios. Public details on capacity and exact campus specifications were not found.

name: Huawei Honghe Prefecture Cloud Computing Big Data Center
developer: Honghe Prefecture / Huawei
notes: Honghe government stated Huawei Honghe Prefecture Cloud Computing Big Data Center started on June 1, 2020 and was able to provide cloud-computing service and host government applications. The Cyberspace Administration of China later noted Honghe launched the Huawei center while building Digital Honghe.

name: Sugon Gejiu Cloud Computing Center
developer: Sugon / Gejiu City
notes: Honghe government said Gejiu signed with Sugon in October 2019 and the cloud-computing big-data center was completed and operational in April 2020 in Datun New District. Phase I included 2000 sqm build area, a 300 sqm data hall, 54 cabinets, 116 servers, T3-standard construction, 12864 CPU cores, 17152 GB memory and 3500 TB storage.

name: Mengzi Green Intelligent Computing Center project
developer: Mengzi City Investment Promotion Bureau / to be determined
notes: Honghe/Mengzi investment-promotion listing describes a green intelligent computing center project in Mengzi's Xinan Suo area, with RMB 158 million estimated investment and 276.25 mu planned area. Honghe's 2025 Digital Honghe work plan separately calls for attracting AI computing centers and deploying edge data centers.

name: SenseTime-Mengzi 1000P AI computing center cooperation
developer: Mengzi City / Shanghai SenseTime Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.
notes: Honghe government reported Mengzi and SenseTime signed a strategic cooperation agreement on March 23, 2026 to promote a 1000P compute-cluster AI computing center and prefecture-wide AI enablement platform, with phase I expected to complete 150P of compute in 2026.

name: China Mobile Digital Two-Asia (Kunming) AI Computing Center
developer: China Mobile Yunnan
notes: People's Daily reported China Mobile Yunnan's single-largest AI computing center had fully entered operation with 17500 PFlops supply capability and a national green data-center B02 building. SASAC earlier reported a thousand-card cluster deployed in Chenggong, and Chenggong district reported the center has 156000 sqm total floor area in three phases and 23500 total installed cabinets.

name: China Telecom Two-Asia International Data Center / Two-Asia AI Computing Center
developer: China Telecom Yunnan
notes: CNR/Yunnan Daily reported the China Telecom Two-Asia International Data Center was completed and put into operation at the end of 2024 and the Two-Asia AI Computing Center was formally operating, with 4000 cabinets and room for 100000 servers. China Telecom later said it had 1200P existing AI compute and was adding 3000P of carrying capacity in Chenggong.

name: Kunming Artificial Intelligence Computing Center
developer: Yunnan Yunshangyun Big Data Industry Development Co., Ltd.
notes: China Daily Yunnan reported the center was first put into operation in January 2023 with 42.24 PFlops FP16, and the data-center building was officially completed and in use on January 25, 2025 in the Yunshangyun 5G Big Data Industrial Park, with about 10000 sqm over four floors, Tier III/CQC A-grade standards, 1000-1200 planned cabinets and about 8192P FP16 planned high-performance compute.

name: Kunming Wanxichong AI Computing Industrial Park
developer: Yunnan Digital Economy Development Zone / multiple operators
notes: Xinhua Yunnan reported Kunming Wanxichong AI Computing Industrial Park was approved as Yunnan's first AI computing industrial cluster. Kunming Information Harbor later said the park includes projects such as Inspur Kunming Cloud Computing Industrial Park, Boyou Computing Data Park and other large compute facilities.

name: Boyou Computing Data Park
developer: Boyou / Yunnan Digital Economy Development Zone stakeholders
notes: Kunming Information Harbor reported the Boyou project in Yunnan Digital Economy Development Zone is building a compute center for 4000 cabinets, including data center, power center and supporting comprehensive building, then in electrical, water/drainage and decoration finishing. Total planned compute is 2000P, with 500P near-term and 1500P long-term.

name: Inspur Kunming Cloud Computing Industrial Park
developer: Inspur
notes: Kunming Information Harbor reported Inspur's Kunming Cloud Computing Industrial Park, in operation since 2017, mainly built the Kunming Cloud Computing Center, big-data application and R&D center, and server/PC production facilities. It had 1200 cabinets in use and provided 20.05 PFlops of general-purpose compute, hosting 523 systems from 53 Kunming municipal units.
